domain_assessment.domain: Military fire-support coordination during a daylight clearing operation
domain_assessment.role: Fire Support Officer (FSO) attached to a company
domain_assessment.objective: Suppress an enemy mortar team and clear a suspected staging compound before the company crosses the line of departure while avoiding friendly-force and village harm
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-available, high-consequence tactical targeting and fire-support decision sequence involving mortar adjustment, competing target reports, danger-close CAS, and artillery approval

decision_points.summary: After two short 81mm mortar adjustment rounds and one clean gun-line check, the FSO chooses to fire a third adjustment round rather than stop for a full re-lay.
evidence_before: Two consecutive adjustment rounds landed short
The section chief performed one check and reported no fault
Most of the approximately 90-minute pre-assault window remained
evidence_after: The third round also landed short
A later fourth check identified a leveling error
goals_constraints: Use available time without delaying the assault
alternatives: Conduct a full re-lay from scratch
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant interpreted the two short rounds as random scatter and believed a hit was due: "Two shorts in a row, felt like we were due for one on target."
decision_points.time_pressure: Reduced. The participant explicitly states that there was enough time for a proper recheck and that time did not drive the decision.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate technical uncertainty about whether the misses reflected random dispersion or a firing-system error.

decision_points.summary: Faced with two similarly confident but conflicting grids for staging activity, the FSO selects the battalion JTAC grid rather than cross-checking the partner-force report.
evidence_before: Partner-force liaison reported Grid B about 300 meters away
The reports had similar stated confidence
Nothing formally established that either report outranked the other
Time was available to verify Grid B
evidence_after: Follow-on reconnaissance found indicators at Grid B as well
goals_constraints: Maintain targeting accuracy near a populated area
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant gave Grid A greater weight because it came through the participant's own FSCC net and from a familiar battalion source rather than because of identified evidentiary superiority.
decision_points.time_pressure: Reduced. The participant says there was time to cross-check and no practical impediment to doing so.
decision_points.uncertainty: High location uncertainty because the reports conflict materially and no source was demonstrably superior.

decision_points.summary: For a danger-close CAS run with unusually tight friendly-force proximity and recent communications dropouts, the FSO clears the attack using the tighter margin rather than delaying for a stable communications check or widening the margin.
evidence_before: The squadron had completed several previous clean strikes
Friendly positions created a tighter-than-usual danger-close margin
Communications with the lead squad had recently dropped intermittently
Time was available to delay without missing the assault
evidence_after: Communications dropped again for approximately ten seconds during the final attack-heading confirmation
Communications returned before the pilot required the call
goals_constraints: Maintain positive coordination with the lead squad
alternatives: Delay for a stable communications check
Clear the strike with the tighter margin
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant extrapolated from the squadron's previous clean record and expected the current run to have the same safe result despite current risk indicators.
decision_points.time_pressure: Reduced. The participant explicitly says a delay was feasible and would not have caused the company to miss the assault.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high execution uncertainty because current communications reliability and friendly-force geometry were worse than in prior strikes.

decision_points.summary: After a single ISR cue of possible enemy activity at the compound, the FSO approves 155mm artillery rather than obtain a second confirming source.
evidence_before: The ISR feed produced one cue of possible enemy activity
The sector had been quiet for the deployment
The area had predominantly normal village pattern-of-life
The sensor had a known false-positive history in this terrain
Time was available to obtain corroboration
evidence_after: Post-strike assessment was mixed and inconclusive regarding whether the compound was occupied
goals_constraints: Clear a suspected enemy staging compound
Avoid unnecessary fires near a village
Act on potentially perishable ISR information
alternatives: Approve the mission from the single ISR cue
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant privileged the case-specific cue because it matched the expected threat: "It matched what we were looking for, so I went with it," while explicitly reporting little reliance on the sector's prior history.
decision_points.time_pressure: Reduced. The participant says the team genuinely had time to seek confirmation.
decision_points.uncertainty: High target-identification uncertainty because the cue was single-source, the sector prior was low, and the sensor's terrain-specific false-positive rate was known.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Two shorts in a row, felt like we were due for one on target.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Mortar-round decision, immediately after the interviewer contrasts a full re-lay with firing another adjustment round.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant forecasts that the next adjustment round is more likely to be on target because the preceding independent rounds were short. The stated belief that a target hit was “due” is a direct sequential-outcome inference rather than a technical diagnosis.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A justified decision to fire again could have rested on an explicit artillery or mortar dispersion model, a documented probability of calibration error, or a technical reason to treat two rounds as insufficient diagnostic evidence. None is supplied; the participant instead explicitly invokes due-ness and admits time was available for a re-lay.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for classification. The direct “due” statement, independent-round context, available alternative, and reduced time pressure are sufficient.

revision.current_defect: No occurrence-level defect. A minor technical-narrative ambiguity remains because the later leveling-error attribution is described as unrelated to the first two misses.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No change required for the bias occurrence. If editing for technical coherence, clarify whether the leveling error was present throughout or arose after the first two rounds without altering the participant's stated belief that the third round was “due.”
preserve: The separate evidence bases of the other three decisions
avoid_creating: A technical explanation that retrospectively makes the third-round decision objectively compelled
A second sequential-outcome bias episode elsewhere
Additional target-bias cues at this decision point

target_occurrence_audit.bias: Ingroup Preference bias or In-group bias
target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I just leaned toward our own channel.” ... “hearing it through your own net makes it feel more solid, even without a concrete reason the information itself was better.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Grid-discrepancy exchange, especially the follow-up hypothetical about the same partner-force report arriving through the participant's own channel.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant differentially weights two otherwise similarly confident reports based on affiliation and familiarity with the participant's own battalion/FSCC channel, while acknowledging no evidentiary reason that the information itself was better.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A familiar source can be rationally preferred if it has superior verified reliability, reporting standards, geolocation practices, or accountability. The interview rules those explanations down by stating that neither source clearly outranked the other and by eliciting the participant's admission that channel affiliation changed perceived solidity without a concrete information-quality reason.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for classification. The source-comparison structure, time to verify, affiliation-based weighting, and channel-switch counterfactual make the mechanism independently observable.

revision.location: Decision point 2, competing Grid A and Grid B exchange.
preserve: Comparable confidence of the two reports
Absence of a documented source hierarchy
The distinction between source affiliation and evidentiary quality
avoid_creating: A formal reliability difference that would make choosing Grid A justified expertise
A second independent source-selection bias at another decision point
An implication that Grid B was known false at the time of decision

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Cleared it hot with the tighter margin. This squadron had been reliable every time, so I expected the same result.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: CAS danger-close decision, followed by the hypothetical that the participant would have used a wider margin and cleaner communications check for a first-time squadron.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant uses a favorable recent record to predict a safe outcome in a current situation with materially worse risk conditions: a tighter-than-normal danger-close geometry and recent communications failures. This underweights present execution risk despite available time to mitigate it.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A strong, well-calibrated prior reliability record may rationally affect a forecast of squadron performance. However, the participant does not describe a quantitative or procedural basis for accepting the changed risk conditions, admits a safer delay was feasible, and says the historical record—not current controls—made the tighter margin acceptable.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for a supported classification. Evidence would only be needed to distinguish a more specific subtype, such as overgeneralization from small samples or a calibration failure.

revision.location: Decision point 3, danger-close CAS clearance exchange.
revision.current_defect: No occurrence-level defect. The occurrence is moderately rather than maximally strong because prior squadron reliability is not inherently irrelevant evidence.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No change required. Do not intensify the language merely to make the bias more explicit.
preserve: The tighter margin and recent communications dropouts
The feasible delay or margin-widening alternative
The absence of an adverse strike outcome
avoid_creating: A claim that the squadron ignored procedures or was unqualified
A second bias based on outcome hindsight

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “That sector had been quiet the whole deployment, mostly normal village pattern-of-life, and that sensor had a track record of throwing false hits in that terrain.” ... “It matched what we were looking for, so I went with it.” ... “I was focused on the cue itself more than the sector's overall track record.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Artillery approval exchange, including the final hypothetical contrasting the cue with the sector's historical activity level.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant approves action from one case-specific cue while discounting two stated prior-probability inputs: low sector-level enemy activity and a sensor-terrain combination with known false positives. The participant explicitly reports that the cue received more attention than the overall base-rate context.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A sufficiently diagnostic real-time cue can rationally outweigh a low base rate, particularly if the cue has strong target-identification characteristics or the threat is highly time-sensitive. The transcript supplies neither a high-likelihood-ratio cue nor time urgency, and it explicitly provides time for corroboration.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for classification. The interview directly establishes the relevant priors, the single cue, the available confirmation option, and the participant's cue-focused weighting.

revision.location: Decision point 4, ISR cue and artillery-approval exchange.
avoid_creating: A claim that confirms the ISR cue was highly diagnostic before the strike
An additional, distinct confirmation-bias episode through new selective-search behavior
A post-strike outcome rationale that replaces the pre-decision reasoning

bias_level_counts.bias: Ingroup Preference bias or In-group bias

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “It matched what we were looking for, so I went with it.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant may have selectively privileged a threat-consistent cue over discordant contextual evidence and a readily available confirming-source check.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This wording can also be fully accounted for by the supported base-rate-neglect mechanism: overweighting a specific cue relative to prior probabilities. The transcript does not establish selective information search, active disconfirmation avoidance, or a prior committed hypothesis strongly enough to count a separate confirmation-bias occurrence.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Grid A ... came through our own FSCC net, format I was used to, source I'd worked with the whole deployment.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: Familiarity with a reporting channel may have functioned as a cue for credibility.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is not independently countable because the same evidence and decision operation are already more specifically and adequately captured by in-group preference. Familiarity may also correlate with genuinely better knowledge of reporting practices, although the interview substantially weakens that defense.

nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Ammunition scarcity is an operational constraint. It could rationally influence the value of re-laying or firing another adjustment round, but the participant does not cite it as the reasoning mechanism for the contested choice.

Communications loss is a real execution-risk indicator, not a cognitive bias. The relevant bias inference comes from the participant's underweighting of that indicator because of the squadron's favorable history.

nonbias_cues.cue: The CAS mission ultimately worked out
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A favorable outcome neither proves nor disproves optimism bias. The occurrence is supported by prospective reasoning before the attack, not by the absence of harm.
An inconclusive outcome does not establish that the original choice was biased or wrong. Base-rate neglect is supported by pre-decision evidence weighting, not by post-strike ambiguity.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant would have stopped after a confirmed gun fault
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This conditional response reflects potentially appropriate contingency-based reasoning. It does not negate the gamblers-fallacy statement made when the fault was not confirmed.

nonbias_cues.cue: Later discovery of indicators at Grid B
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Subsequent corroboration at Grid B is not evidence that choosing Grid A was wrong. The in-group bias classification rests on the participant's contemporaneous affiliation-based source weighting.

causal_claims.claim: The available 90-minute window did not materially alter the participant's processing at the four central decision points.
causal_claims.support: The participant repeatedly states that time was available to re-lay, cross-check, delay CAS, and obtain a second ISR source, then concludes that extra time did not change how the situation was read.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as a self-report of decision process, but not as a demonstrated causal estimate relative to the paired 30-minute scenario.

causal_claims.claim: A leveling error caused or contributed to the later short mortar round.
causal_claims.support: The participant says a fourth check identified a leveling error after the third round was also short.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible but technically under-specified. The statement that the error was “unrelated to the first two misses” creates ambiguity about whether it existed at the time of the third round and how it causally explains the sequence.

causal_claims.claim: The squadron's prior clean record caused the participant to accept the tighter CAS margin.
causal_claims.support: The participant directly says the track record made the tighter margin feel acceptable and would have chosen differently for a first-time squadron.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as a reported causal influence on the participant's judgment.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Prior squadron reliability may be a valid predictive factor rather than proof of unwarranted optimism.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The current danger-close geometry and communications conditions are explicitly worse, and a no-cost delay was available; the interview therefore supports risk underweighting rather than treating prior reliability itself as irrational.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The later discovery of indicators at Grid B could invite retrospective inference that the original Grid A selection was erroneous.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The transcript provides the participant's pre-decision reason for source weighting and does not rely on the later outcome to establish bias.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The mixed post-strike assessment could invite outcome-based labeling of the artillery choice as biased.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The base-rate-neglect finding is grounded in the participant's stated pre-strike weighting of one cue over known priors.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Duration of the pre-assault time window: the paired scenario's 30-minute window is specified as changed to a 90-minute window.
held_constant: Ammunition limitations for the 81mm mortar section
Intermittent communications degradation between FSCC and forward observers
Danger-close proximity of friendly squads to the compound
Possible civilian presence in the adjacent village
Single ISR feed with known false-positive history
The four decisions, alternatives, sequence, and intended reasoning mechanisms
causal_audit.explanation: The interview consistently establishes that the changed condition is reduced time pressure and actively probes whether additional time would have enabled a safer or more evidentially grounded alternative. The participant consistently reports that time was available but did not drive the four central choices. However, the paired 30-minute transcript is not supplied, so the audit can assess internal fidelity to the declared counterfactual condition but cannot independently verify that every listed non-time variable was held constant across versions. The mortar leveling-error wording is also a minor causal-narrative ambiguity, not a defect in the gamblers-fallacy evidence.

global_revision_constraints: Do not use the favorable or unfavorable outcomes to retroactively justify the four bias classifications.
Preserve the four distinct decision points and their non-overlapping evidence sources.
Preserve reduced time pressure as the only declared counterfactual change.
If a technical edit is made, clarify the mortar leveling-error timeline without removing the explicit independent-round “due” inference.
Do not turn the additional confirmation-bias and familiarity-heuristic candidates into separate occurrences unless the manifest is intentionally expanded.
